```{r load-data}
repo <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChrisSimoneau/HCIN5400/"
gdp_table <- read.csv(paste0(
  repo, "de40a22a8386e69549ad1f7a46ae0a8a65c7da1c/",
  "gdp_annual_and_statistics_by_country.csv"
))
gdp <- data.frame(country_code = gdp_table$Code, mean_usd = gdp_table$Mean)

accidents <- read.csv(paste0(
  repo, "c1dc63208652d0264e16dddd2d9525d455a9dd08/",
  "accident_rate_by_country_2002_2023.csv"
), check.names = FALSE)

head(gdp[c("country_code", "mean_usd")])
head(accidents[c("Country Code", "Accidents_per_million")])
```

```{r merge-data}
# Join by country code and keep all economies in the accident data.
combined <- merge(
  accidents,
  gdp[c("country_code", "mean_usd")],
  by.x = "Country Code",
  by.y = "country_code",
  all.x = TRUE
)

# Check the first six rows of the merged data.
head(combined[c("Country Code", "mean_usd", "Accidents_per_million")])

# List economies without a usable GDP value.
missing_gdp <- combined[
  is.na(combined$mean_usd),
  c("Country Code", "Country Name")
]
missing_gdp
```

```{r plot-gdp-accident-rate}
# Keep rows with a positive GDP and an available accident rate.
plot_data <- subset(
  combined,
  is.finite(mean_usd) & mean_usd > 0 & is.finite(Accidents_per_million)
)

# Plot one point per economy.
plot(
  plot_data$mean_usd / 1e9,
  plot_data$Accidents_per_million,
  log = "x",
  pch = 19,
  col = "steelblue",
  xlab = "Average GDP (current US$ billions, log scale)",
  ylab = "Accidents per million departures"
)
```

```{r gdp-accident-correlation}
# Measure the rank correlation between GDP and the accident rate.
rho <- cor(
  plot_data$mean_usd,
  plot_data$Accidents_per_million,
  method = "spearman"
)

nrow(plot_data)
round(rho, 3)
```

## Results

Across the 174 economies with usable data, average GDP and recorded
aviation accidents per million departures had a weak positive rank
correlation (Spearman's rho = 0.231). This describes an association
across economies and does not establish a causal effect of GDP.

## Higher vs. lower GDP comparison

I split the matched economies at the median of their 2002–2023 average GDP. Economies at or above the median are in the higher GDP group. For each group, I divided total accidents by total departures and multiplied by one million.

```{r compare-gdp-groups}
cutoff <- median(plot_data$mean_usd)
plot_data$GDP_group <- ifelse(plot_data$mean_usd < cutoff,
                             "Lower GDP", "Higher GDP")

totals <- aggregate(cbind(Accidents, Departures) ~ GDP_group,
                    data = plot_data, FUN = sum)
totals$Economies <- as.integer(table(plot_data$GDP_group)[totals$GDP_group])
totals$Accidents_per_million <- round(totals$Accidents / totals$Departures * 1e6, 3)
knitr::kable(totals)
```

The median average GDP was about US$41.9 billion. Each group had 87 economies. The lower GDP group had 2.528 recorded accidents per million departures and the higher GDP group had 0.347, a difference of 2.181 per million departures.

### Average GDP and aviation accidents for five countries

Each row shows one country's average annual GDP, total recorded aviation accidents, and accident rate for 2002–2023.

```{r five-country-gdp}
codes <- c("USA", "RUS", "IDN", "NPL", "CAN")
five <- combined[match(codes, combined[["Country Code"]]), ]
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Country = five[["Country Name"]],
             Average_GDP = five$mean_usd / 1e9,
             Recorded_Accidents = five$Accidents,
             Accident_Rate = five$Accidents_per_million),
  digits = c(0, 1, 0, 3), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  col.names = c("Country", "Average annual GDP, 2002–2023 (current US$ billions)",
                "Recorded accidents, 2002–2023",
                "Accidents per million departures, 2002–2023")
)
```
